title: Secrets are read through one vendor-agnostic manager client interface
description: The project imports a single Secrets Manager client that exposes the named verbs `get(name)`, `getRequired(name)`, `list()`, and `refresh()`. `get` returns the current value or null; `getRequired` throws a stable-coded error on absence; `list` returns the manifest-declared name set for this process; `refresh` re-reads every secret this process is authorised for. The client is the sole importer of the vendor binding on the boundary; no other module reaches for the vendor SDK, an environment variable, or a config file directly. The default vendor is named in ADR-902; the interface itself does not depend on which vendor is behind it. The Secrets Manager client is what the blueprint contributes as the `secretsProvider` capability: it is the sole surface the project uses to read a secret value at runtime, and the applied capability set exposes the token so consumer blueprints (the auth blueprints, the delivery blueprints) can bind against it rather than accessing the vendor SDK directly.
rationale: A vendor-agnostic port keeps the project free to change vendors under a passing test suite. It also removes the class of bugs where two modules read the same secret through two different code paths and disagree about whether it is set. One client, one boundary, one behaviour.
